subject: maths
title: Equations with unknowns on both sides

scenes.heading: Unknowns on both sides
scenes.sub: When do two gyms cost the same?
scenes.say: Gym A costs forty-five dollars to join plus twelve dollars a week. Gym B costs twenty-one dollars a week. When do they cost the same? To find out, you need equations with x on both sides.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Lift 2 bags off EACH pan and the scale still balances
scenes.science: Subtract the same x-term from both sides to collect the unknowns
scenes.breaks: A real bag can't hold a negative number of marbles, but x can be negative or a fraction.
scenes.say: Picture a balance with five bags of marbles and three loose marbles on one pan, and two bags with eighteen marbles on the other. Lift two bags off each pan and it still balances. That is exactly how you gather the unknowns on one side.

scenes.heading: The method
steps: Remove the smaller x-term from both sides
Move the numbers to the other side
Divide by the number in front of x
scenes.say: Here is the method. Remove the smaller x term from both sides, so the x term left over is positive. Move the numbers to the other side. Divide by the number in front of x. Then check your answer in both sides of the original equation.

scenes.heading: Example 1
scenes.question: Solve 5x + 3 = 2x + 18.
scenes.say: Solve five x plus three equals two x plus eighteen. Subtract two x from both sides: three x plus three equals eighteen. Subtract three: three x equals fifteen. Divide by three: x equals five. Check: both sides give twenty-eight.
scenes.caption: Solve 5x + 3 = 2x + 18. Subtract 2x from both sides: 3x + 3 = 18. Subtract 3: 3x = 15. Divide by 3: x = 5. Check: both sides give 28.

scenes.heading: Example 2: a negative x-term
scenes.question: Solve 7 − 2x = 3x − 8.
scenes.say: Now seven minus two x equals three x minus eight. The smaller x term is negative two x, so add two x to both sides: seven equals five x minus eight. Add eight: fifteen equals five x. So x equals three.
scenes.caption: Now 7 − 2x = 3x − 8. The smaller x-term is −2x, so add 2x to both sides: 7 = 5x − 8. Add 8: 15 = 5x. So x = 3.

scenes.heading: The gym problem
scenes.question: Gym A: $45 + $12 a week. Gym B: $21 a week. When equal?
scenes.say: Back to the gyms. Gym A is forty-five plus twelve w, and Gym B is twenty-one w. Set them equal. Subtract twelve w: forty-five equals nine w. So w is five. After five weeks, both cost one hundred and five dollars.
scenes.caption: Back to the gyms. Gym A is 45 + 12w, and Gym B is 21w. Set them equal. Subtract 12w: 45 = 9w. So w = 5. After 5 weeks, both cost $105.

scenes.heading: When x disappears
scenes.say: Sometimes the x terms cancel. Three x plus five equals three x minus one becomes five equals negative one. That is false, so there is no solution. But two x plus six equals six plus two x becomes six equals six. Always true, so every number works.
scenes.caption: Sometimes the x-terms cancel. 3x + 5 = 3x − 1 becomes 5 = −1. That is false, so there is no solution. But 2x + 6 = 6 + 2x becomes 6 = 6. Always true, so every number works.

points: Do the same to both sides
Answers can be negative or fractions
scenes.say: Quick recap. Always do the same to both sides. Remove the smaller x term first. Answers can be negative or fractions. And check in both sides of the original equation. Now try the practice questions!
